task: Run Team T acceptance from an isolated Git worktree after the provenance merge.
observation: The first acceptance attempt failed before testing because the ignored repository-local moss executable was absent from the new worktree, while the runner resolves the compiler at that worktree's repository root.
impact: Each validation worktree required its own compiler build before package runners could execute, adding a setup cycle but not changing SDK or compiler correctness.
evidence: margo: error: command failed (.../moss build --json): [Errno 2] No such file or directory

resolution.summary: Build ./moss in every detached validation worktree before invoking Margo-based acceptance runners.

suggestion: Document that ignored repository-local compiler binaries are worktree-local prerequisites for isolated validation.

task: Determine whether Foundations expression lowering and Team M mixed numeric lowering coexist after the automatic src/moss.cpp merge.
observation: The focused imported-generic regression gate exercised nested calls, indexed literals, field projections, native execution, Fast Debug, and source-free ABI-v9 providers, while Team M package tests exercised both mixed Int/Float operand directions. Together they validated the shared merge without reconstructing a duplicate package proof campaign.
impact: Team I could keep review proportional to the actual shared-compiler risk and found no compiler or ABI integration defect.

resolution.summary: All focused combined-compiler and source-free ABI-v9 checks passed at the integrated implementation SHA.

task: Merge the final Team M and Team T review tips into phase24-integration and run the complete regression matrix.
observation: Git normal merges preserved both Team histories; the only conflicts were historical status/review ledgers. The merged source passed the root regression suite, examples, all Math/Random/Time/integration package tests, Text/Encoding package tests, and the full Text/Encoding acceptance corpus.
impact: The compiler-first gates and package drivers provided direct evidence that the final source tips integrated without a cross-package or shared-compiler regression.

resolution.summary: Final Team M and Team T tips are merged as normal commits and validated at ee4973f5556b3cd07204e877157e35fd49ad1874.

tool_used: Git, Moss, Margo, and package acceptance runners

task: Run the complete Team N package matrix after merging the corrected numerics delivery.
observation: Launching all Margo package suites concurrently caused intermittent missing-object linker errors because package builds shared repository-local artifacts; rerunning the same suites serially passed in native debug, Fast Debug, and release modes.
impact: Parallel orchestration is not reliable for these package targets, but the serial validation establishes the integrated source is correct and the limitation does not indicate a compiler or package defect.
evidence: parallel Margo package matrix: missing object/linker errors in linalg, statistics, and numerics integration

resolution.summary: Serial reruns passed all affected suites; package validation is recorded as serial for reproducibility.

task: Run Team D structured-data acceptance from the combined integration checkout.
observation: The accepted Team D runners hard-coded a different historical checkout path, so the documented acceptance command could not run from this clone until the root was derived from the script location.
impact: The defect was in validation orchestration rather than SDK behavior; it blocked reproducible in-place acceptance until corrected.

resolution.summary: Both runners now derive the repository root path; package, source-free, and differential checks execute against the combined tree.

task: Run focused R0 compiler regressions after fetching the updated integration baseline.
observation: The first same-module type-resolution probe used the ignored repository-local compiler binary from before the fetched R0 source changes and reproduced the old vector type mismatch; rebuilding ./moss was required before the regression could validate the merged source.
impact: The stale binary created a false initial failure and an avoidable setup cycle, but the rebuilt compiler passed both R0 focused suites.

resolution.summary: Rebuilt ./moss from the fetched source; type-resolution and bitwise regressions then passed.

task: Validate Team D nested JSON semantic behavior after integrating Team H.
observation: The existing validity and Python differential suites accepted nested JSON, but a minimal Moss probe inspecting child IDs, object keys, lookups, and compact serialization exposed interleaved descendant corruption: [[1],2] became [[1],1], and {"a":{"x":1},"b":2} lost b before a vector-bounds failure.
impact: Parsing-success coverage was insufficient to establish semantic correctness; the focused probe classified a high-severity package defect without changing Team I's JSON implementation.

resolution.summary: P24-D-003 is returned to Team D; moss.json is RED pending a repaired exact-SHA implementation and independent Architect GO.

tool_used: Margo Fast Debug and semantic JSON API probe

task: Integrate Team D corrective delivery and validate nested container and differential behavior on the combined tree.
observation: Merging Team D's independently approved corrective delivery (reviewed at 6ef17f1c2edc1022f00f77a35bec051b1b9cdab3, tip db5f6663e94f3711db3b55a611d13f1508f97368) resolved P24-D-003: [[1],2], {"a":{"x":1},"b":2}, compact/pretty round-trips, control characters, and INT64_MIN format all pass in Native and Fast Debug; the differential test suite passed 103/103 cases.
impact: P24-D-003 nested container corruption is resolved on the combined integration tree without regressively affecting any existing SDK packages or compiler features.

resolution.summary: Team D's corrective delivery is integrated; P24-D-003 is resolved; all repository gates pass.

tool_used: Git, Moss, Margo, and data-acceptance runner

task: Merge and validate Team A (Advanced Data) and Team R (Data Utilities) deliveries into the Phase 24 aggregate SDK tree.
observation: Sequential non-fast-forward 3-way merges integrated all 5 Team A packages (ndarray, datastructures, tables, binary, cbor) and 4 Team R packages (hash, compress, regex, data_utils_integration). All 9 packages passed serial three-mode testing (Native Debug, Native Release, Fast Debug: 111 Team A tests x 3 = 333 executions, 36 Team R tests x 3 = 108 executions) and end-to-end acceptance oracles with 100% parity.
impact: The aggregate Phase 24 SDK tree now includes all approved deliveries from Teams C, T, M, N, D, H, A, and R, coexisting cleanly with zero compiler, runtime, or cross-package regressions.

resolution.summary: All 9 newly integrated packages pass three-mode execution and combined acceptance gates.

tool_used: Git, Moss, Margo, and package acceptance runners
